issues.t: Valve seat drops out and damages the engine
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping that gets louder, then a sudden misfire, rough running and loss of compression, usually on cylinder 4 and at high mileage.
issues.why: On the 2.0L single-cam engine a valve seat can work loose from the aluminum cylinder head, often after the engine has run hot. The loose seat can wreck the valve, piston and head.
issues.next: If a new ticking appears or the engine suddenly runs on three cylinders, stop driving and have a compression test done. Keep the cooling system in good shape to lower the risk.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, the engine revving between shifts, harsh or late shifts, or the car losing drive.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic in these Escorts wears out internally, and failures are among the most-reported problems from about 55,000 miles on.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. Have the transmission diagnosed before it fails completely; a used or rebuilt unit is usually the most practical fix on an older Escort.

issues.t: Shifting problems or won't go into gear
issues.sym: The car is slow to engage or will not move in Drive or Reverse, or shifts erratically.
issues.why: Owners of 2000 and 2001 Escorts report shifting problems and transmissions that stop engaging, often from worn internal clutches or shift solenoid trouble.
issues.next: Check the fluid first, then have the codes and line pressure checked by a transmission shop.

issues.t: Engine runs rough or misfires
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, stumbling when accelerating, or a check engine light for misfires.
issues.why: Worn spark plugs and wires, a weak ignition coil, vacuum leaks or a dirty idle air control valve are common causes on these engines. On high-mileage engines a dropped valve seat can also cause it.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Start with plugs, wires and the coil, which are inexpensive, before assuming engine damage.

issues.t: Rough idle (ZX2)
issues.sym: The idle speed hunts up and down, feels rough, or the engine nearly stalls at stops.
issues.why: RepairPal lists rough idle as a known ZX2 complaint. A dirty or failing idle air control valve or a vacuum leak is the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the idle air control valve cleaned or replaced and the intake checked for vacuum leaks.

issues.t: Engine knocking at high mileage
issues.sym: A deep knock from the engine that gets louder with speed or load.
issues.why: Owners report bottom-end knocking on high-mileage engines, usually from worn bearings, often after low oil or overheating.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away. A knock that does not go away usually means the engine needs rebuilding or replacing.

issues.t: Whistling or noise from the PCV valve
issues.sym: A whistle, hiss or rattle from the top of the engine, sometimes with a rough idle.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve or its hose can fail and leak vacuum.
issues.next: Have the PCV valve and hose checked; they are cheap parts.

issues.t: Engine stutters or struggles when starting
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, sputters or takes several tries to start.
issues.why: Owners of 1999 Escorts report hard and rough starts, which can come from ignition, fuel delivery or idle control problems.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure, ignition and stored codes checked so the right part gets replaced.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks and engine quits
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving and cranks but will not start.
issues.why: Owners report timing drive failures around 110,000 miles. When the belt that turns the camshaft breaks, the engine stops immediately.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt on schedule if there is no record of it being done. If it has snapped, have the valves checked before just fitting a new belt.

issues.t: Check engine light on
issues.sym: The check engine light stays on, sometimes with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Owners of these years often report the light from emissions sensors such as oxygen or EGR sensors, or ignition faults.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a parts store or shop; many causes are inexpensive.

issues.t: Automatic seat belts get stuck
issues.sym: The motorized shoulder belt stops partway or will not move along its track.
issues.why: The 1996 Escort uses motorized shoulder belts that run on a track in the door frame. The motor or track wears and jams.
issues.next: Have the track and motor repaired so the belt works properly; buckle the lap belt in the meantime.

issues.t: Battery won't hold a charge
issues.sym: Slow cranking or a dead battery after sitting.
issues.why: Owners report batteries that drain, from an aging battery, a weak alternator or a small electrical drain.
issues.next: Have the battery, alternator and parasitic drain tested.

issues.t: Air bag light on from contaminated monitor (recall)
issues.sym: The air bag readiness light comes on. In very rare cases there could be melted wiring, a fire or an unexpected air bag deployment.
issues.why: Contamination in the air bag monitor could cause faults. Ford recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the air bag light diagnosed.

issues.t: Replacement seat belts may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. A replacement seat belt may not lock in a crash.
issues.why: A small batch of TRW replacement seat belt assemblies used for repairs could fail to lock. It was recalled.
issues.next: If your belts were ever replaced, check your VIN and the recall to see if yours are affected.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not latch fully (recall)
issues.sym: A buckle seems latched but releases, or will not latch firmly.
issues.why: Some seat belt buckles may not properly restrain an occupant in a crash. Ford recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and test each buckle with a firm tug.

issues.t: Shift indicator may not show the right gear (recall)
issues.sym: The gear position shown does not match the gear the car is in.
issues.why: On some cars the shift lever pattern did not meet the federal standard, so drivers could not tell which gear they were in. Ford recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and always confirm Park before getting out.

issues.t: Brakes fail or the pedal goes soft
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks or the car takes much longer to stop.
issues.why: Owners of 1999 Escorts report brake failures, which can come from leaking lines, a failing master cylinder or worn parts.
issues.next: Do not drive with a soft pedal. Have the brake fluid, lines and master cylinder inspected right away.

issues.t: Front rotors wear out before the pads
issues.sym: Grinding, pulsing in the pedal, or a vibration when stopping even with good pads.
issues.why: Owners report thin front rotors that warp or wear out early.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced with quality parts.

issues.t: Transmission differential fails
issues.sym: Whining or clunking from the transmission area, then loss of drive.
issues.why: Owners report the differential inside the automatic transaxle failing around 96,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop driving when you hear a new grinding or clunk. A used or rebuilt transaxle is usually needed.

issues.t: Alternator burns out
issues.sym: Battery light, dim lights, a dead battery or a burning smell.
issues.why: Owners of 2003 cars report alternator failures around 69,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested and replace the alternator before the battery is drained.

issues.t: Car stops moving in Reverse
issues.sym: The car will not back up, or stops moving when put in Reverse.
issues.why: Owners report loss of Reverse at low mileage, which points to an internal transmission fault.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the transmission diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: Rear end sways over bumps
issues.sym: The rear of the car feels loose or sways side to side over bumps.
issues.why: Worn rear shocks, struts or bushings let the rear move around.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected and replace worn parts in pairs.

issues.t: Control relay module failure stops A/C or fan
issues.sym: The A/C stops blowing cold, the radiator fan does not run, or the engine overheats in traffic; in some cases the car will not start.
issues.why: These Escorts use one relay module for the A/C clutch, cooling fan and fuel pump. RepairPal names its failure the most-reported Escort problem.
issues.next: Have the constant control relay module tested. Replacing it is usually quick, and watch the temperature gauge until then.
